Projects.title: LifeLink
desc: LifeLink is a blood donation mobile application designed to help people quickly find blood donors and blood banks during emergencies. The project was inspired by the difficulties a friend faced while arranging blood during a critical situation.

The design process included user research, user flows, paper wireframes, low-fidelity wireframes, and high-fidelity prototypes. The goal was to simplify the process of finding donors, submitting blood requests, and connecting with nearby blood banks.
The final prototype focused on accessibility, ease of navigation, and reducing the time required for users to respond to urgent blood requests.

caseStudy.title: The Problem
content: During medical emergencies, finding blood donors quickly can be difficult. Existing methods often rely on personal networks, social media posts, and manual coordination, leading to delays when time is critical.
The goal of LifeLink was to create a centralized platform that enables users to locate blood donors, discover nearby blood banks, and respond to urgent requests with minimal friction.

caseStudy.title: Personalized Home Dashboard
caseStudy.content: The home screen provides immediate access to urgent requests, donation actions, and nearby resources while maintaining a simple and accessible navigation structure.

caseStudy.title: Donation Confirmation Flow
caseStudy.content: The donation flow helps users verify eligibility and review request information before confirming their participation.

caseStudy.title: Blood Bank Discovery
caseStudy.content: Users can search nearby blood banks and access relevant information when immediate assistance is required.

caseStudy.title: Profile & Impact Tracking
caseStudy.content: The profile section enables users to manage personal information, view donation history, and track their contributions.

caseStudy.title: Reflection
content: This project strengthened my understanding of designing for high-pressure situations where users need information quickly and decisions must be made with confidence.
Future improvements include real-time donor matching, location-based notifications, blood inventory integration, and emergency alert systems.

Projects.title: Fam Manager
desc: Fam Manager is a family management platform designed to help families organize important documents, schedules, and events in one secure place. The idea originated from personal challenges in managing family records and appointments.
The project involved user research, information architecture, paper wireframes, low-fidelity wireframes, mobile and web interface design, and high-fidelity prototypes.
The final solution enables families to securely store documents, manage schedules, organize events, and access important information through an intuitive user experience.

caseStudy.title: The Problem
content: Families often struggle to keep important documents, schedules, and records organized across multiple locations and platforms.
The goal of Fam Manager was to create a centralized solution that enables families to securely manage documents, appointments, events, and essential information in one place.

Projects.title: AgroVision
desc: AgroVision is a precision farming platform designed to help farmers make informed decisions using soil, weather, and crop health data. The project focused on simplifying complex agricultural information into a clear and actionable user experience.

The platform integrates GIS data, Google Earth Engine, NDVI analysis, and machine learning techniques to provide crop health monitoring, environmental insights, and farm management support through interactive dashboards.

The project was published at IEEE ICCAMS 2025 and demonstrates the application of AI-driven agricultural analytics, geospatial technologies, and user-centered design to support data-informed farming decisions.

caseStudy.title: The Problem
content: Modern farming generates large amounts of environmental and crop-related data, but most farmers lack accessible tools to convert that information into actionable insights.
The goal of AgroVision was to create a platform that combines GIS, NDVI analysis, weather information, and machine learning into a single intuitive dashboard.

caseStudy.title: Select your coordinates using the map or enter the values manually
Impact
content: AgroVision demonstrates how AI, geospatial technologies, and data visualization can be combined to support precision agriculture.
The project was published at IEEE ICCAMS 2025 and highlights the value of user-centered design in agricultural technology solutions.

Projects.title: Retail Demand Forecasting & Inventory Intelligence
desc: Retail Demand Forecasting & Inventory Intelligence is a machine learning platform designed to estimate next-day sales across retail stores and product families using historical sales, promotions, and time-based patterns.
The project combines time-series feature engineering with LightGBM to analyze historical sales and generate store- and product-specific sales estimates through a Flask API and React dashboard.
The final tuned LightGBM model achieved a validation RMSLE of 0.3763 using lag features, rolling statistics, calendar features, and promotion data.

caseStudy.title: The Problem
content: Retail businesses struggle to accurately predict sales across different stores and product categories.
Changes in customer demand, seasonality, promotions, and past sales patterns make inventory planning difficult.
The challenge was to build a machine learning solution that could use historical sales data to predict next-day sales and support better inventory decisions.

caseStudy.title: Exploratory Data Analysis
content: The dataset contains daily sales records across 54 stores and 33 product families from 2013 to 2017.
Analysis revealed long-term sales growth, strong weekly seasonality, large differences between product families and stores, and a relationship between promotion activity and sales.

caseStudy.title: Feature Engineering
content: The forecasting pipeline uses calendar features, historical lag values, and rolling statistics calculated separately for each store and product family.
Lag features include 1, 7, 14, 28, and 365 days, while rolling 7-day and 28-day statistics capture recent sales behavior. Historical features are shifted before calculation to prevent target leakage.

caseStudy.title: Model Development
content: Multiple models were evaluated using chronological validation, including Seasonal Naive, Linear Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM.

LightGBM was progressively tuned across tree complexity, learning rate, estimator count, and regularization parameters. The final configuration used 128 leaves, a 0.04 learning rate, 1,500 estimators, and a log-transformed sales target.

caseStudy.title: Results
content: The tuned LightGBM model achieved a validation RMSLE of 0.3763 and RMSE of 219.57.
The model was retrained on the combined processed training and validation data and exposed through a Flask inference API.

caseStudy.title: Dashboard
content: The React dashboard allows users to select a store, product family, and promotion count, then generate a next-day estimated sales value.
Historical recorded sales are displayed alongside supporting 7-day and 30-day statistics, while the model estimate is highlighted as the primary output.

caseStudy.title: Reflection
content: This project strengthened my understanding of time-series forecasting, leakage prevention, model evaluation, feature engineering, and deploying machine learning models through APIs.
Future improvements include recursive multi-day forecasting, automated promotion inputs, inventory-aware demand estimation, and richer forecasting uncertainty analysis.

Projects.title: F1 Race Winner Prediction
desc: F1 Race Winner Prediction is a machine learning system designed to estimate a driver's probability of winning a Formula 1 race using historical race, qualifying, driver, constructor, championship, and circuit data.
The project combines feature engineering with tuned CatBoost and XGBoost classification models and exposes predictions through a Flask API with an interactive React dashboard.
The dashboard makes the prediction process transparent by displaying the 36 engineered features used by the model before presenting the predicted win probability.

caseStudy.title: The Problem
content: Formula 1 race outcomes depend on many interacting factors, including qualifying performance, starting position, driver form, constructor strength, and championship position.
The goal was to build a machine learning system that could combine these signals and estimate a driver's probability of winning a race.

caseStudy.title: Feature Engineering
content: The system builds a per-driver-per-race feature table from historical F1 datasets.

The final model uses 36 engineered features covering race information, starting position, qualifying performance, driver historical performance, driver championship statistics, constructor performance, and constructor championship statistics.
Historical driver and constructor statistics are calculated using information available before the corresponding race to reduce target leakage.

caseStudy.title: Model Development
content: CatBoost and XGBoost classification models were trained to predict whether a driver would win a race.
The application supports both tuned models through the same prediction interface.

caseStudy.title: Prediction
content: Users select a driver, race, and prediction model. The backend retrieves the corresponding engineered feature row and passes the 36 features to the selected model in the same order used during training.
The result is presented as a win probability together with key race, qualifying, driver, and constructor information.

caseStudy.title: Reflection
content: This project strengthened my understanding of feature engineering, classification, historical sports data, model evaluation, API development, and building transparent machine learning interfaces.
A key focus was making the model inputs visible so users can understand which factors contribute to each prediction.

Projects.title: FinFlow AI
desc: FinFlow AI is an AI-powered financial operations platform designed to help freelancers and independent professionals streamline invoice processing and financial reconciliation.

The platform combines document processing, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and AI-assisted workflows with a deterministic reconciliation engine to match invoices and payments, identify discrepancies, and support financial operations.

Built with React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Prisma, LangChain, Ollama, and FAISS, the project explores reliable financial automation through exact and fuzzy matching, payment allocation, and intelligent document analysis.

caseStudy.title: The Problem
content: Freelancers and independent professionals often manage invoices, bank transactions, and financial records across different platforms. Manually matching payments with invoices can become time-consuming and error-prone as financial records grow.
FinFlow AI was developed to explore how AI-assisted document processing and automated reconciliation could simplify financial operations while maintaining accuracy, transparency, and human oversight.

caseStudy.title: Dashboard Overview
content: The Overview dashboard provides a snapshot of the workspace's financial activity.

It displays key indicators including total invoices, payment completion, paid invoice value, outstanding balances, transaction count, and open exceptions, helping users quickly understand their financial position.

caseStudy.title: Reconciliation Engine
content: The reconciliation engine compares invoice records against imported bank transactions and generates proposed invoice-to-transaction matches.

It uses matching logic to identify potential allocations and duplicate candidates. Reconciliation runs save proposed matches without immediately changing invoice payment statuses, allowing financial updates to remain controlled until allocations are approved.

caseStudy.title: Allocation Review
content: The Allocations dashboard provides a review interface for proposed invoice-to-bank transaction matches.

Users can inspect invoice details, vendors, transaction references, amounts, invoice statuses, and allocation statuses. Approving an allocation updates the corresponding invoice payment status and creates an audit record, while rejected allocations preserve the review history.

caseStudy.title: Transaction Management
content: The Transactions dashboard displays imported bank transaction records with their descriptions, references, dates, debit or credit direction, amounts, and currencies.
These records serve as the financial data source for reconciliation, helping users identify relevant payments and compare them against recorded invoices.

caseStudy.title: Invoice Management
content: The Invoices dashboard centralizes vendor invoice records and provides visibility into invoice amounts, issue dates, due dates, payment statuses, and outstanding balances.
It helps users monitor payment progress and identify invoices that require review or reconciliation.

caseStudy.title: Exception Handling
content: The Exceptions section provides a dedicated workflow for reviewing reconciliation issues such as potential duplicate transactions, unmatched records, and discrepancies.
Users can investigate flagged cases, record resolution notes, and track exception status changes to ensure unresolved financial issues receive attention.

caseStudy.title: Audit & Traceability
content: The Audit Log maintains a historical record of important workspace activities and system events.

It captures actions such as reconciliation runs, allocation approvals or rejections, and exception resolutions, along with associated entities and event details. This provides traceability and supports transparent financial workflows.

caseStudy.title: AI-Powered Financial Assistant
content: The AI Assistant enables users to ask questions about their workspace's financial information using natural language.

Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) allows the assistant to retrieve relevant financial context and reference uploaded financial documents. Its read-only functionality keeps AI interactions separate from financial operations.

caseStudy.title: Document Processing
content: The Documents section allows users to upload financial documents such as invoices in PDF format.

Uploaded files are processed and indexed into a workspace-specific vector store, enabling document retrieval through the AI Assistant. The interface displays document names, file types, processing statuses, and upload timestamps.

caseStudy.title: Technical Architecture
content: FinFlow AI uses a modular architecture with a React and TypeScript frontend, Node.js and Express backend, PostgreSQL database, and Prisma ORM.
Financial reconciliation is handled through a dedicated TypeScript engine, while LangChain, Ollama, and FAISS support AI-assisted document retrieval and financial analysis.

A key architectural decision was to separate deterministic financial operations from AI-generated responses. This helps maintain predictable reconciliation behavior while allowing AI to assist with document understanding and information retrieval.

caseStudy.title: Reflection
content: FinFlow AI strengthened my understanding of financial data processing, backend architecture, AI integration, document retrieval, and the importance of deterministic business logic in AI-assisted applications.
Future improvements include enhanced reconciliation confidence scoring, human approval workflows, stronger audit controls, improved document extraction accuracy, and expanded financial analytics.
